html:
The Carnatic was the plain of south east India along the Coromandel Coast, ruled in the 1700s by the Nawabs of Arcot. On the 1783 and 1800 maps it is a state the British controlled in all but name.

The nawabs began as Mughal governors under the Nizam of Hyderabad. In the 1740s and 1750s the British and French fought each other here through rival claimants to the throne, in the Carnatic Wars. The British side, led in part by Robert Clive, won, and their man Muhammad Ali Khan Wallajah ruled from 1749 to 1795.

He borrowed huge sums from Company officers at high interest, and the scandal of the nawab's debts reached Parliament in London. In 1780 Hyder Ali of Mysore swept through the Carnatic and laid it waste. In 1801 the East India Company took over its government, and the land became part of the Madras Presidency around Madras.
